newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebels kill four police in southwest Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Rebels kill four police in southwest Colombia.

text.p: Leftist rebels killed at least four policemen in a pre-dawn attack on Friday in a small town in southwest Colombia and reduced the local police station to rubble, authorities said.

Spokesmen for National Police Chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano said two other policemen were wounded in the attack by about 100 Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels and two more were officially listed as missing.

Agents holed up in the police station in Barbacoas in a rural area of Narino province held off the rebels for several hours until they finally ran out of ammunition, the police spokesmen said, adding that the building was eventually destroyed by rocket-propelled grenades and heavy gunfire.
They said more police might have been killed in the attack but army reinforcements forced the guerrillas to pull out of Barbacoas soon after it had fallen into their hands.

A police report issued in March said 4,617 police had been killed in Colombia since 1990, more than anywhere else in the world. Most died in attacks by leftist guerrillas led by the FARC, the country's biggest rebel group, and the smaller National Liberation Army.
